problem: `defaultWords` prints the base `defaultThreshold` whenever the two effective window defaults are equal, even when both differ from the base. Since 2.0 the Settings window never writes the base: `SettingsThresholdDefaults` calls `appState.setDefaultWindowThreshold` for each slider (`SettingsView.swift:94-99`). So equal window defaults that differ from the base are a normal state. In that state `pixelswitch status` shows a default that auto-switch does not use, and contradicts the `accounts` table printed by the same CLI.
failure_scenario: On the Beeco Mac (base 98), drag both Settings sliders to 95, or run `settings set autoSwitch.sessionThreshold 95` and `settings set autoSwitch.weeklyThreshold 95`. `pixelswitch status` prints `Auto-switch:   on, default 98%, next by most room left`, but auto-switch leaves at 95%, and `pixelswitch accounts` prints `95% (default)`. I reproduced this by compiling CLIRunner.swift with AutoSwitchInfo(defaultThreshold: 98, defaultSessionThreshold: 95, defaultWeeklyThreshold: 95).

problem: Spec 5.7 rule 2 says: "Every scratch test, `remote-control.sh` included, checks `testMode: true` first." Lane MB is the only lane that may edit this file (lanes.md:46). LC runs the script but cannot edit it (lanes.md:49 and 69). The 2.0 edit changed only 18 to 20 tools, so the guard ships missing and no later lane can add it. The script refreshes usage, starts a real sign-in and changes two settings on whatever daemon answers.
failure_scenario: On the founder's laptop after the real 2.0 install, LC (or a 2.1 lane) runs `PIXELSWITCH_CLI=<linux cli> bash Tests/integration/remote-control.sh` with a scratch HOME and XDG_RUNTIME_DIR, while the scratch daemon is down. The Linux client walks spec 5.2's fallback list to `/run/user/<uid>/pixelswitch/control.sock`, which is the real daemon. The script then sends `usage.refresh` with the CabDesign farm's live login, starts the real `claude auth login`, and writes and restores settings on the live daemon. Because PIXELSWITCH_NO_LAUNCH is not set, it may also run `systemctl --user start`, which spec 5.7 rule 5 forbids before release.
fix:
Right after the first `status` call, refuse a Linux daemon that is not in test mode. The Mac app sends no `platform` or `macos`, so Mac runs are unaffected:
```bash
if status=$("$CLI" --json status); then
    if [ "$(echo "$status" | field platform)" = "linux" ] && [ "$(echo "$status" | field testMode)" != "True" ]; then
        echo "Refusing: this Linux PixelSwitch is not in test mode (spec 5.7). Run it only against a scratch daemon."; exit 2
    fi
    [ "$(echo "$status" | field protocolVersion)" = "2" ] && ok "status answers, protocol 2" || bad "status protocol" "$status"
```
`field` prints Python's `True` for JSON true. Also export `PIXELSWITCH_NO_LAUNCH=1` when the platform is linux.

problem: The new `UserDefaults.didChangeNotification` pipeline is created inside the `@MainActor` `ControlEventHub` with no `.receive(on:)`. Under SWIFT_VERSION 6.0 (project.yml:23), its `map` and `sink` closures are main-actor isolated and carry a runtime isolation check. The notification is posted on the thread that wrote the default, so any write to any defaults from a background thread, by any code or framework in the process, traps the app. The hub exists from launch to quit. No such writer was found in the app's own code today (Sparkle was not checked), so the risk is latent. `follow(_:)` at line 177 already guards its own pipeline with `.receive(on: DispatchQueue.main)`.
failure_scenario: A scratch program with this exact pipeline (a @MainActor class, the same map/prepend/removeDuplicates/dropFirst/sink chain, compiled with -swift-version 6) died with SIGTRAP (exit 133) when `UserDefaults.standard.set` ran on `DispatchQueue.global()`. The same write on the main queue was fine. In the app, such a write would quit PixelSwitch, and with it the control socket and auto-switch.
fix:
Hop to main before any isolated closure runs, as `follow(_:)` does:
```swift
NotificationCenter.default.publisher(for: UserDefaults.didChangeNotification)
    .receive(on: DispatchQueue.main)
    .map { _ in DefaultFields.current }
```
The same scratch program with `.receive(on: DispatchQueue.main)` ran clean (exit 0) and the event arrived on main.

problem: The `get_settings` description, written in this change, tells the model that `autoSwitch.sessionThreshold` and `autoSwitch.weeklyThreshold` take "null/\"default\" to follow autoSwitch.threshold". But `run` treats a null in any required argument as missing (line 202: `arguments[key] == nil || arguments[key] == .null`), and `set_setting` requires `value`. So null never reaches the app, and the description promises something the MCP refuses. The spec's rule that null clears these keys is reachable through the CLI and the socket, but not through MCP.
failure_scenario: An AI follows the description and calls `tools/call set_setting {"key":"autoSwitch.sessionThreshold","value":null}`. It gets `invalidParams: set_setting needs value.`, a misleading message, and the app is never called (reproduced in a scratch build of MCPServer.swift; `"default"` worked).
fix: Let a JSON null through for `set_setting`'s `value` only, keeping the absent check: `for key in tool.required where arguments[key] == nil || (arguments[key] == .null && !(tool.name == "set_setting" && key == "value"))`. Add a test that `set_setting` with `value: null` forwards `{"key":...,"value":null}`. If you would rather keep the guard, drop `null/` from the `get_settings` description and say `"default"` only.

problem: `orderSet` always adds "Every account is now numbered from 1 in this order, replacing any priority numbers you set." A 1.9 app's `accounts.setOrder` numbers nothing. During the update gap (new CLI in the updated bundle, old app process still running), the sentence is false, and the table printed above it shows `—` in every Priority cell.
failure_scenario: Sparkle has replaced the bundle, but the 1.9 process still serves the socket. `pixelswitch accounts order 2 1 3` prints the new order with every Priority `—`, then claims every account is now numbered from 1.
fix: Pass the status to it, as `.priority` already does: in `execute` call `CLIOutput.orderSet(Self.accounts(result["accounts"]), numbered: app.features?.contains(ControlProtocol.featurePriority) == true)`, and append the sentence only when `numbered` is true. Add a check in `runOldAppTests` with the stand-in 1.9 app answering `accounts.setOrder`.

problem: Spec section 4 says "The `account` descriptions say 'an email, label or position, never a priority number'". The shared `account` property does, but `get_usage`'s `account` (line 62, "Optional: only this account.") and `start_sign_in`'s `account` (line 72, "Optional: re-sign this account instead of adding a new one.") do not. The test at ControlSplitTests.swift:419-422 checks only four tools, so the gap is not caught.
failure_scenario: With priorities P1, P3 and P9 (positions 1, 2, 3), an AI asked to re-sign "my P3 account" calls `start_sign_in {"account":"3"}`. That resolves to position 3, the P9 account, and starts a re-sign of the wrong account.
fix: Use the same words in both, e.g. `"Optional: only this account (an email, label, id or position, never a priority number)."` and `"Optional: re-sign this account (an email, label, id or position, never a priority number) instead of adding a new one."`. Extend the test's tool list to every tool that has an `account` property: `tools.filter { $0["inputSchema"]?["properties"]?["account"] != nil }`.

problem: The new controls have no accessible name. The Priority stepper and both window steppers are Stepper("") with .labelsHidden(), so VoiceOver reads them as an unnamed stepper. The Priority menu is announced only as "P1" or "None". The Session and Weekly menus (lines 155-171) are announced only by their label, so two side-by-side pop-ups both say "Default (90%)". The "Session", "Weekly" and "Priority" captions are separate static text, not the controls' labels.
failure_scenario: A VoiceOver user tabs through a row and hears "Default (90%), pop-up button" twice, then "stepper" with no name. They cannot tell which pop-up sets the 5-hour limit and which sets the weekly limit, or what the stepper changes.
fix: Give each stepper a real label and keep it visually hidden, which leaves it available to VoiceOver: `Stepper { Text("Priority") } onIncrement: {...} onDecrement: {...}.labelsHidden()` at line 137, and `Stepper { caption } onIncrement: ... onDecrement: ...` at line 176. On the Priority Menu add `.accessibilityLabel(Text("Priority"))`. On each window Menu add `.accessibilityLabel(caption)` plus `.accessibilityValue(...)` set to the same Text the label shows ("Manual only", "Switch at N%" or "Default (N%)"). The keys "Priority", "Session" and "Weekly" already exist in all five tables.

problem: Each Session and Weekly column is a fixed frame 164pt wide (line 184) holding a .fixedSize() menu plus a stepper. That width fits English (measured from the render: the "Switch at 90%" pop-up is 135pt, plus 4pt spacing and a 20pt stepper, 159pt in all). The German label "Wechseln bei %lld%%" is about 30pt wider in 13pt SF, so the content is about 188pt. A frame(width:) does not grow to fit, so the content draws past it. French "Par défaut (100 %)" is also slightly over. The renders cover English only. These widths are estimates from glyph metrics, because this Mac cannot render SwiftUI.
failure_scenario: With the app in German, an account with its own session limit (for example after picking 90% in Session) shows "Wechseln bei 90%" and its stepper running about 24pt past its column. With only 10pt of spacing, that is about 14pt drawn over the left edge of the Weekly pop-up. In the Weekly column the stepper runs past the row's trailing edge.
fix: Size the column for the widest of the five tables, not for English. Raising windowColumnWidth to about 196 covers "Wechseln bei 100%" plus the stepper. Alternatively, measure the widest label once with a PreferenceKey and share that width across rows. Then render one German row to confirm. The window is 820pt wide, so an address still keeps 28 or more characters.

problem: Every click on the priority stepper calls setPriority, and setPriority re-sorts the list at once. Equal numbers go to the account set most recently, so a row can move out from under the pointer between two clicks. The next click then lands on another account's stepper.
failure_scenario: After a drag, A is P1, B is P2 and C is P3. The user clicks A's up arrow three times. Click 1: A becomes P2 and stays first (set most recently). Click 2: A becomes P3 and the list becomes B, A, C, so row 1 is now B. Click 3 lands on B's stepper: B becomes P3 and sorts first. The user meant to give A P4 but changed B's number without noticing.
fix: Do not move the row while someone is stepping through numbers. One option is to drop the priority stepper and make every number a deliberate menu pick: keep None and P1-P9, and add submenus 10-19 through 90-99. Another is for SettingsAccountsTab to hold the pending number in @State, show it in the row, and call appState.setPriority only after a short pause, for example 0.8 s with no further click.

problem: The split-window help sentence always adds "(up to X of its week when no account under its weekly limit can take you)". When the session limit is lower than the weekly limit, the relaxed weekly limit is max(weekly, session), which equals the weekly limit, so X equals the weekly number already stated.
failure_scenario: An account set to Session 50 and Weekly 90 shows the tooltip "...and moves you to it only while it is at 49% or less of its session and 89% or less of its week (up to 89% of its week when no account under its weekly limit can take you)." The extra clause suggests a different limit where there is none.
fix: Add the parenthetical only when numbers.relaxedArriveWeekly > numbers.arriveAt.weekly. Otherwise return a new sentence without it: "Auto-switch moves you off this account at %@ of its session or %@ of its week, and moves you to it only while it is at %@ or less of its session and %@ or less of its week." Add that key to all five tables and to the key list in runSplitStringTests.

problem: This is a latent threading risk outside the views, found while checking for run-time isolation problems. ControlEventHub is @MainActor and the app builds in Swift 6 mode. The .map and .sink closures on NotificationCenter.default.publisher(for: UserDefaults.didChangeNotification) are formed in the @MainActor init, so the Swift 6 compiler treats them as main-actor-isolated and inserts a run-time check that traps if they run on another thread. UserDefaults.didChangeNotification is posted on whichever thread changed a default. Every in-repo write today is on the main actor (AppState, SettingsStore, MenuBarConfig), so this does not fire now.
failure_scenario: Any in-process defaults write from a background thread would trap the app on that thread (a dispatch queue assertion) the moment remote control is running. That could be a framework such as Sparkle, or future code that persists a flag from a Task or a URLSession callback.
fix: Hop to the main queue before any closure runs: `NotificationCenter.default.publisher(for: UserDefaults.didChangeNotification).receive(on: DispatchQueue.main).map { _ in DefaultFields.current } ...`.

problem: When the two window defaults are equal, defaultWords prints the base `autoSwitch.threshold` instead of the effective window defaults. The test at Tests/UnitTests/ControlSplitTests.swift:371-376 only uses base = session = weekly = 98, so it cannot catch this.

The user moves both new sliders to 80 (or runs `settings set autoSwitch.sessionThreshold 80` and `autoSwitch.weeklyThreshold 80`), and the base stays at 90 (unset) or at 98 on the Beeco Mac. `pixelswitch status` then prints `Auto-switch:   on, default 90%, ...`, while `pixelswitch accounts` prints `80% (default)` and auto-switch leaves at 80%. Confirmed with a scratch probe compiled from the shipped CLI files.
fix: In defaultWords, replace `return percent(a.defaultThreshold)` with `return percent(a.defaultSessionThreshold ?? a.defaultThreshold)`. Add a test: AutoSwitchInfo(defaultThreshold: 90, defaultSessionThreshold: 80, defaultWeeklyThreshold: 80) must make the status line contain `default 80%`.

problem: Spec section 4 says the `account` descriptions say they are 'never a priority number'. get_usage (line 62, 'Optional: only this account.') and start_sign_in (line 72, 'Optional: re-sign this account instead of adding a new one.') do not. problem: The check labelled 'half away from zero' uses 49.5, which also rounds to 50 under round-half-to-even. So it cannot tell the two rule sets apart, and spec section 4 requires half away from zero. The same blind spot covers the settings keys: 72.4 at line 189 is not a .5 case.
